topic: Seasons have nothing to do with distance from the Sun
lesson: A season is decided by the angle sunlight hits the ground at, not by how far away the Sun is, so the two hemispheres can feel opposite seasons on the very same day.

post.caption:
Earth is closest to the Sun in January, and that's still the middle of winter. Distance barely changes all year. What actually decides the season is the tilt of the axis, aiming sunlight straight down on one hemisphere and spread thin on the other.
